docs.title: Vexy JSON
docs.text:
Vexy JSON is a forgiving JSON parser written in Rust. It reads standard JSON and the relaxed syntax found in hand-written configuration files and in text produced by language models, and it returns ordinary JSON values.

The same parser is available as a Rust library, a command-line tool, a Python package, a WebAssembly module and a C library.

docs.title: What it accepts
docs.text:
Standard JSON parses unchanged. On top of that, the default settings accept:

  • //, /* … */ and # comments
  • trailing commas in arrays and objects
  • unquoted object keys and unquoted single-word string values
  • single-quoted strings
  • implicit top-level objects (a: 1, b: 2) and arrays (1, 2, 3)
  • newlines in place of commas
  • hexadecimal (0x1F), octal (0o17) and binary (0b101) integers, and underscores in numbers (1_000)

Each extension can be switched off. See Accepted syntax and Parser options.

docs.title: One example
docs.text:
This input is not valid JSON:

// service settings
{
  name: 'cache',
  ports: [8080, 8081,],
  retries: 0x3
}

Vexy JSON turns it into this value:

{
  "name": "cache",
  "ports": [8080, 8081],
  "retries": 3
}

The comment is dropped, the unquoted key and the single-quoted string become ordinary strings, the trailing comma is ignored and the hexadecimal number becomes a decimal integer.

Interface Package Entry point Rust library vexy-json on crates.io vexy_json::parse Command line vexy-json-cli on crates.io vexy-json binary Python vexy-json on PyPI import vexy_json Browser and Node.js built with wasm-pack from crates/wasm parse_json C and C++ vexy-json-c-api (static and dynamic library) vexy_json_parse

docs.title: Try it in the browser
docs.text: The interactive demo runs the WebAssembly build of the parser in your browser. Type relaxed JSON on the left and the normalized JSON appears on the right. An older version of the demo is kept at demo/legacy.html.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: This page describes how the repository is organized and how a string becomes a value. It is meant for contributors and for users who need to know why the interfaces behave as they do.

docs.title: Workspace layout
docs.text:
The repository is one Cargo workspace. The root package vexy-json is the facade crate; the other crates live in crates/:

Path Crate Role crates/core vexy-json-core Lexers, parsers, errors, repair, streaming, parallel and transform modules crates/cli vexy-json-cli The vexy-json binary (clap, tokio, rayon, notify) crates/python vexy-json-python PyO3 extension, packaged with maturin as vexy-json on PyPI crates/wasm vexy-json-wasm wasm-bindgen exports for JavaScript crates/c-api vexy-json-c-api C ABI and the vexy_json.h header crates/serde vexy-json-serde SerdeValue wrapper crates/test-utils vexy-json-test-utils Helpers for the test suite src/ vexy-json Re-exports from the core and Serde crates

Other top-level directories:

  • tests/ — integration tests for the root crate
  • examples/ — small runnable programs (cargo run --example simple)
  • benches/ — Criterion benchmarks
  • fuzz/ — cargo-fuzz targets
  • scripts/ — WebAssembly build, release and packaging scripts
  • src_docs/ — this documentation site

All crates share one version number. scripts/release-manifests.py check verifies that every manifest carries the same version.

docs.title: From text to value
docs.text: Take the input {a: 1, b: [2,],} and follow it through parse.

docs.title: 1. Choosing a lexer
docs.text: Parser::new looks at the options. If any of the six syntax options is on, it uses FastLexer. The lexer runs in forgiving mode when allow_comments is on and in strict mode when it is off. If all six syntax options are off, the parser uses Lexer, a tokenizer generated with the logos crate.

docs.title: 2. Tokens
docs.text:
The lexer turns the text into tokens, each with a Span (start and end byte offset). The parser reads the token text back through the span:

LeftBrace  UnquotedString  Colon  Number  Comma
UnquotedString  Colon  LeftBracket  Number  Comma  RightBracket
Comma  RightBrace  Eof

Spaces are dropped. Comments arrive as SingleLineComment and MultiLineComment tokens, which the parser skips. Newlines arrive as Newline tokens, so that newline_as_comma can treat them as separators.

docs.title: 3. Parsing
docs.text:
The parser is a recursive descent parser. It keeps a depth counter in ParserState and stops with DepthLimitExceeded when the depth reaches max_depth. For the example it:

  1. sees { and starts an object;
  2. reads the unquoted key a (allowed by allow_unquoted_keys), the colon and the number 1;
  3. reads the key b and an array; inside it, the comma before ] is a trailing comma (allowed by allow_trailing_commas);
  4. accepts the comma before } for the same reason;
  5. returns Value::Object with the members a → Integer(1) and b → Array([Integer(2)]).

At the top level, the parser checks for a key followed by : (implicit object) or a value followed by a comma (implicit array) when implicit_top_level is on. After the value, any further token other than the end of input is an error.

docs.title: 4. Numbers
docs.text: Number tokens are converted to Number::Integer(i64) when they are integers that fit, including hexadecimal, octal, binary and underscore forms, and to Number::Float(f64) otherwise.

docs.title: The fallback chain
docs.text: parse_with_fallback wraps the parser in three tiers: serde_json for strict JSON, then the forgiving parser, then a bracket repairer when enable_repair is on. The result records which tier succeeded. The CLI calls this function with repair turned off, and adds its own end-of-input repair on top (see Repairing incomplete input).

docs.title: How each interface converts the value
docs.text:
The core returns Value. Each interface converts it differently, which explains some of their differences:

Interface Conversion CLI Its own formatter, with string escaping, compact or indented Python Builds dict, list and scalar objects directly WebAssembly Prints Value with Display, re-reads it with serde_json, prints compact JSON C Serializes Value with its derived Serde implementation (tagged form)

Because Display does not escape strings, the WebAssembly round trip fails on strings with escaped quotes or control characters. See Troubleshooting.

Script or workflow Purpose build.sh Full local gate: format, Clippy, build, tests, doctests, examples, Python wheel and tests, documentation build.sh docs Documentation only (calls src_docs/build.sh) scripts/build-wasm.sh Builds the WebAssembly module into src_docs/md/pkg/ publish.sh Tags a release and publishes the crates and the Python package .github/workflows/ci.yml Tests on pushes and pull requests .github/workflows/release.yml On a v* tag: tests, then builds CLI binaries, the macOS installer and the WebAssembly archive for the GitHub release .github/workflows/docs.yml On pushes that change src_docs/ or the WebAssembly sources: rebuilds this site into docs/

GitHub Pages serves the docs/ folder of the main branch at https://vexy.dev/vexy-json/.

docs.title: C and C++
docs.text: The vexy-json-c-api crate exposes the parser through a C ABI. Cargo builds it as a static library and a dynamic library named vexy_json_c_api. The declarations are in crates/c-api/include/vexy_json.h.

docs.title: Building and linking
docs.text:
Prerequisites: a Rust toolchain and a C compiler.

  1. Build the library in release mode:

    cargo build --release -p vexy-json-c-api

  2. Compile your program against the header and link the static library. On macOS:

    cc -I crates/c-api/include example.c \
  target/release/libvexy_json_c_api.a \
  -framework CoreFoundation -o example

    Other platforms need other system libraries. This command prints the list for your platform:

    cargo rustc -p vexy-json-c-api --lib --crate-type staticlib -- --print native-static-libs

  3. Run ./example.

docs.title: A complete example
docs.text:
#include <stdio.h>
#include "vexy_json.h"

int main(void) {
    printf("vexy_json %s\n", vexy_json_version());

    VexyJsonParseResult r = vexy_json_parse("{a: 1, b: [true, 'x'],}");
    if (r.error) {
        fprintf(stderr, "error: %s\n", r.error);
    } else {
        printf("%s\n", r.json);
    }
    vexy_json_free_result(r);

    VexyJsonParserOptions options = vexy_json_default_options();
    options.allow_unquoted_keys = false;
    r = vexy_json_parse_with_options("{a: 1}", &options);
    printf("error: %s\n", r.error);
    /* error: Expected string key but found UnquotedString at position 2 */
    vexy_json_free_result(r);
    return 0;
}

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
Function Purpose const char* vexy_json_version(void) Library version; do not free VexyJsonParserOptions vexy_json_default_options(void) Options with every extension on VexyJsonParseResult vexy_json_parse(const char* input) Parse with default options VexyJsonParseResult vexy_json_parse_with_options(const char* input, const VexyJsonParserOptions* options) Parse with options; NULL options means defaults VexyJsonDetailedResult vexy_json_parse_detailed(const char* input, const VexyJsonParserOptions* options) Same parse, in the detailed result type VexyJsonParser vexy_json_parser_new(const VexyJsonParserOptions* options) Create a reusable parser handle VexyJsonParseResult vexy_json_parser_parse(VexyJsonParser parser, const char* input) Parse with a handle's options void vexy_json_parser_free(VexyJsonParser parser) Free a handle void vexy_json_free_result(VexyJsonParseResult result) Free both strings of a result void vexy_json_free_detailed_result(VexyJsonDetailedResult result) Free a detailed result

VexyJsonParserOptions has the fields listed in Parser options. max_depth and max_repairs are uint32_t; the other fields are bool.

docs.title: Results and memory
docs.text:
A VexyJsonParseResult holds two strings:

  • json: the parsed value, or NULL on error
  • error: the error message, or NULL on success

Exactly one of them is set. A NULL input gives the error Input is null; input that is not UTF-8 gives Invalid UTF-8 input.

The library allocates both strings. Release every result with vexy_json_free_result exactly once, and do not use its pointers afterwards. Do not pass them to free().

A parser handle is not thread-safe. Create one handle per thread, and free it with vexy_json_parser_free.

docs.title: Output format
docs.text:
The json string is produced by Serde's derived serialization of the Rust Value enum, so it keeps the enum variant names instead of plain JSON:

{"Object":{"a":{"Number":{"Integer":1}},"b":{"Array":[{"Bool":true},{"String":"x"}]}}}

Each value is an object with one key naming its kind: Null, Bool, Number (containing Integer or Float), String, Array or Object. Read it with a JSON library and unwrap one level per value. Member order in Object is not kept.

docs.title: Current limitations
docs.text:
• vexy_json_parse_detailed does not track repairs yet: repairs is always NULL and repair_count is 0.
  • The repair fields of VexyJsonParserOptions have no effect; the C functions never repair input.
  • crates/c-api/include/vexy_json.hpp, a C++17 wrapper, refers to type names that the C header does not define (for example vexy_json_parse_result), so it does not compile with the current header. From C++, include vexy_json.h directly; it has extern "C" guards.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
The vexy-json program reads relaxed JSON from files or standard input and writes standard JSON. It is built from the vexy-json-cli crate.

vexy-json [OPTIONS] [FILE]...

With no FILE, the program reads standard input. With several files, it processes them one after another (or in parallel with --parallel) and writes each result in turn.

docs.title: How a run works
docs.text:
For each input, vexy-json:

  1. Reads the bytes and checks that they are valid UTF-8. Invalid UTF-8 is an error that names the byte where decoding stopped.
  2. Parses the text. It first tries a strict JSON parser (serde_json) and, if that fails, the forgiving Vexy JSON parser with the options from the command line.
  3. On success, formats the value and writes it to standard output or to the --output file.
  4. On failure, prints Error: and the message to standard error and exits with status 1. With --repair, it first tries to close truncated input (see Repairing incomplete input).

docs.title: Output options
docs.text:
Option Effect -o, --output <FILE> Write the result to FILE instead of standard output -p, --pretty Indent the output --indent <INDENT> Spaces per indentation level (default 2) -c, --compact Write everything on one line with no extra whitespace -v, --validate Check the input and print Valid JSON instead of the value

Without --pretty or --compact, objects and arrays are indented and scalars (strings, numbers, booleans, null) are written on one line. No newline is added after the output.

With --validate and more than one file (or in watch mode), each line names the file: settings.conf is valid JSON.

docs.title: Syntax options
docs.text:
Each flag switches off one extension. They map to the parser options of the same name.

Flag Disables --no-comments //, # and /* … */ comments --no-trailing-commas trailing commas --no-unquoted-keys unquoted object keys --no-single-quotes single-quoted strings --no-implicit-top-level objects and arrays without outer braces or brackets --no-newline-as-comma newlines as separators --max-depth <MAX_DEPTH> maximum nesting depth (default 128)

docs.title: Input modes
docs.text:
Option Effect --ndjson Treat the input as newline-delimited JSON: one value per line --parallel-parse Parse one large input with the parallel parser --chunk-size <CHUNK_SIZE> Minimum chunk size in bytes for parallel parsing (default 65536) --max-threads <MAX_THREADS> Thread limit for parallel parsing; 0 means automatic (default 0) -j, --parallel Process several input files at the same time -w, --watch Process the files, then reprocess each one when it changes --lms Run lms ls --json --llm and parse its output

--chunk-size and --max-threads apply to both --parallel-parse and --ndjson.

In --ndjson mode each value is written separately. With --pretty, values are separated by a blank line.

--watch needs at least one file. It prints Watching N files for changes... (Press Ctrl+C to stop) and keeps running until you stop it.

--lms is for the LM Studio command-line tool. It runs lms ls --json --llm, captures the complete output in a temporary file (256 MiB at most) and parses it. It cannot be combined with file arguments, --watch, --parallel, --repair, --parallel-parse or --ndjson.

docs.title: Error and repair options
docs.text:
Option Effect --verbose-errors Report the line and column of a parse error and show the lines around it -r, --repair Close input that ends inside open objects or arrays, and warn about it --repair-details Requires --repair; the repair report is the same as with --repair alone --fallback Accepted for compatibility; the strict-then-forgiving fallback always runs

--repair cannot be combined with --watch, --ndjson or --parallel-parse.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Parse a file and pretty-print it with four-space indentation:

vexy-json --indent 4 config.json5

Write the normalized, compact result to a new file:

vexy-json -c settings.conf -o settings.json

Check several files at once:

vexy-json -v a.conf b.conf

a.conf is valid JSON
b.conf is valid JSON

Find the line of a syntax error:

vexy-json --verbose-errors bad.conf

Error:
Parse error in file 'bad.conf' at line 4, column 9: Expected , or ] or newline but found Some((Colon, Span { start: 36, end: 37 })) at position 37

   3     list: [1, 2
   4 >   other: 3
              ^
   5   }

Without --verbose-errors the message is one line: bad.conf: Expected , or ] or newline … at position 37.

Reject anything that is not strict JSON:

vexy-json --no-comments --no-trailing-commas --no-unquoted-keys \
  --no-single-quotes --no-implicit-top-level --no-newline-as-comma data.json

docs.title: Exit status
docs.text: Status Meaning 0 All inputs parsed (or were empty) 1 A file was missing, the input was not UTF-8, parsing failed or a repair was unsafe 2 Invalid command-line arguments, such as --repair together with --ndjson

docs.title: Other options
docs.text: Option Effect -h, --help Print help; -h prints a summary -V, --version Print the version

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Git
  • A Rust toolchain with cargo, rustfmt and clippy
  • uv (provides uv and uvx) and python3
  • For the WebAssembly module: the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and wasm-pack
  • For the WebAssembly smoke test: Node.js

docs.title: Getting the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-json.git
cd vexy-json

docs.title: Running the full gate
docs.text:
build.sh in the repository root is the canonical check. Run it before you open a pull request:

./build.sh

It performs these steps in order and stops at the first failure:

  1. Checks that git, cargo, rustc, uv, uvx and python3 are present and that the expected project files exist.
  2. Runs scripts/release-manifests.py check to confirm that all manifests carry the same version.
  3. Runs cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy -D warnings on the CLI crate.
  4. Builds and tests the workspace (except the Python crate), including doctests and examples.
  5. Builds the Python wheel with uv build, installs it in a temporary virtual environment, runs crates/python/tests with pytest and a smoke test that compares vexy_json.__version__ with the workspace version.
  6. Builds this documentation site in strict mode into a temporary directory.
  7. Fails if the build changed any tracked or untracked file in the checkout.

The output is also written to build.log.txt. The last line is BUILD SUCCESS: … or BUILD FAILURE: ….

docs.title: Working on the documentation
docs.text:
The documentation sources are Markdown files in src_docs/md/. The site configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme into docs/, which GitHub Pages serves.

  1. Edit or add a page in src_docs/md/. Add new pages to the nav list in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

  2. Preview the site:

    src_docs/build.sh serve

    The preview runs at http://127.0.0.1:8000 and reloads on save.

  3. Build the site:

    ./build.sh docs

    This runs src_docs/build.sh, which builds in strict mode: any warning, such as a broken link between pages, fails the build. The result replaces the contents of docs/.

Do not edit files in docs/ by hand; the next build overwrites them. The .github/workflows/docs.yml workflow rebuilds docs/ on every push to main that changes src_docs/ or the WebAssembly sources, and commits the result.

docs.title: The demo and the WebAssembly bundle
docs.text:
The browser demo lives in src_docs/md/demo/, with its scripts and styles in src_docs/md/assets/. The WebAssembly bundle it loads lives in src_docs/md/pkg/. ProperDocs copies these files to docs/ unchanged.

To rebuild the bundle after changing crates/core or crates/wasm:

  1. Run ./scripts/build-wasm.sh release. The script writes the new bundle to src_docs/md/pkg/.

  2. Run the smoke test against it:

    mkdir -p crates/wasm/pkg
cp src_docs/md/pkg/* crates/wasm/pkg/
node crates/wasm/test.mjs

    The test prints All tests passed! at the end. Delete crates/wasm/pkg/ afterwards.

  3. Rebuild the site with ./build.sh docs.

docs.title: Code guidelines
docs.text:
• Keep the forgiving behaviour behind ParserOptions so that every extension can be switched off.
  • Add a test in tests/ for each syntax change. The existing files are grouped by topic, such as comment_handling.rs, number_formats.rs and newline_as_comma.rs.
  • When a change affects a binding, update its tests: crates/python/tests/ for Python and crates/wasm/test.mjs for WebAssembly.
  • Record user-visible changes in CHANGELOG.md under Unreleased.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text:
Maintainers release with ./publish.sh. According to the README, the script verifies the repository boundary, checkpoints intended changes, runs the full build, creates and verifies the release tag, then publishes the workspace crates in dependency order followed by the Python package (built with uv build, uploaded with uv publish).

Pushing the v* tag starts .github/workflows/release.yml, which tests the tagged source, builds the CLI binaries, the macOS installer and the WebAssembly archive, and attaches them to the GitHub release.

Interrupted releases

Registry uploads cannot be undone. If publication stops after the tag was created, check crates.io and PyPI before retrying, and resume only the uploads that are missing. Do not rerun the whole script: it derives the next version from the existing tags.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Vexy JSON ships as several packages built from one Cargo workspace. Install the one that matches the language you work in. All packages share one version number.

docs.title: Rust library
docs.text:
Prerequisites: a Rust toolchain with Cargo.

  1. Add the crate to your project:

    cargo add vexy-json

    Or add it to Cargo.toml by hand:

    [dependencies]
vexy-json = "1"

  2. Build the project with cargo build.

The vexy-json crate re-exports the parser from vexy-json-core. Its default serde feature also pulls in vexy-json-serde. To build without it, turn off default features:

[dependencies]
vexy-json = { version = "1", default-features = false }

The workspace publishes these crates to crates.io:

Crate Contents vexy-json High-level crate that re-exports the parser API vexy-json-core Lexer, parser, repair, streaming and transform modules vexy-json-cli The vexy-json command-line program vexy-json-serde SerdeValue, a Serde wrapper around Value vexy-json-wasm WebAssembly bindings (built with wasm-pack) vexy-json-c-api C ABI, built as a static and a dynamic library

docs.title: With Cargo
docs.text:
1. Install the CLI crate:

    cargo install vexy-json-cli

  2. Check the installation:

    vexy-json --version

    The command prints the program name and version, for example vexy_json 1.5.13.

docs.title: From a GitHub release
docs.text:
Each tagged release on the releases page carries prebuilt binaries:

  • vexy-json-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz and …-linux-aarch64.tar.gz
  • vexy-json-<version>-macos-x86_64.tar.gz, …-macos-aarch64.tar.gz, a universal …-macos.zip and a …-macos.dmg installer
  • vexy-json-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip

Unpack the archive and put the vexy-json binary (vexy-json.exe on Windows) on your PATH.

docs.title: From a source checkout
docs.text:
install.sh in the repository root builds the CLI and installs it under ~/.local (the binary goes to ~/.local/bin). It also builds and installs the Python extension; see below.

./install.sh                 # CLI under ~/.local
./install.sh --prefix /opt   # CLI under /opt instead

The prefix can also come from the VEXY_JSON_PREFIX environment variable.

docs.title: Python package
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Python 3.8 or later. The PyPI distribution is named vexy-json; the import name is vexy_json.

uv add vexy-json          # in a uv-managed project
uv pip install vexy-json  # into the active environment
pip install vexy-json     # with pip

Check the installation:

python -c "import vexy_json; print(vexy_json.__version__)"

The package contains a compiled extension module (vexy_json._vexy_json) built from crates/python with maturin and PyO3. If no prebuilt wheel exists for your platform, the installer builds it from the source distribution, which needs a Rust toolchain.

./install.sh in a source checkout builds a wheel for the system Python selected by uv python find --system --no-managed-python and installs it with uv pip install --system.

docs.title: WebAssembly module
docs.text:
The WebAssembly bindings are not published to npm. Use one of these sources:

  • Release archive. Each GitHub release has a vexy-json-wasm-<version>.tar.gz asset with the wasm-pack output (pkg/).
  • Hosted copy. The documentation site serves the current build at https://vexy.dev/vexy-json/pkg/vexy_json_wasm.js. The demo loads it from there.

  • Build it yourself. Prerequisites: Rust with the wasm32-unknown-unknown target and wasm-pack.

    1. Run the build script from the repository root:

      ./scripts/build-wasm.sh release

    2. Collect the output from src_docs/md/pkg/: vexy_json_wasm.js, vexy_json_wasm_bg.wasm, the TypeScript declarations and package.json.

The build uses wasm-pack build --target web, so the module is an ES module with a default init export. See JavaScript and WebAssembly.

docs.title: C and C++ library
docs.text:
Prerequisites: a Rust toolchain and a C or C++ compiler.

  1. Build the library:

    cargo build --release -p vexy-json-c-api

    Cargo writes libvexy_json_c_api.a and the platform's dynamic library (libvexy_json_c_api.dylib, .so or .dll) to target/release/.

  2. Add crates/c-api/include to your include path. It holds vexy_json.h, which C and C++ code can include.

  3. Link against the library. See C and C++ for an example.

docs.title: Parser options
docs.text: Every interface reads the same set of options. In Rust they are the fields of vexy_json::ParserOptions; the Python, WebAssembly and C bindings expose the same names. With the defaults, every syntax extension is on.

docs.title: Option reference
docs.text:
Option Type Default Effect when true allow_comments bool true Accept //, # and /* … */ comments allow_trailing_commas bool true Accept a comma after the last array element or object member allow_unquoted_keys bool true Accept object keys without quotes allow_single_quotes bool true Accept strings in single quotes implicit_top_level bool true Accept a: 1 as {"a": 1} and 1, 2 as [1, 2] newline_as_comma bool true Accept a newline in place of a comma max_depth integer 128 Maximum nesting depth of arrays and objects enable_repair bool true Let parse_with_fallback try bracket repair after a parse error max_repairs integer 100 Upper limit on repairs that the repairer attempts fast_repair bool false Use the repairer without its cache report_repairs bool true Reserved; the parser does not read it in this version

The three repair options affect only parse_with_fallback (Rust) and the functions built on it. Plain parse and parse_with_options never repair input. See Repairing incomplete input.

docs.title: How strict mode works
docs.text:
Switching the six syntax options off makes the parser behave like a strict JSON parser. Take this input:

{a: 1}

With the defaults it parses to {"a": 1}. With allow_unquoted_keys set to false, the parser stops at the key and reports:

Expected string key but found UnquotedString at position 1

The position is a zero-based byte offset into the input.

allow_comments also controls the lexer mode

When allow_comments is false but another syntax option is still on, the lexer runs in strict mode. Strict mode rejects unquoted words and single-quoted strings even if allow_unquoted_keys or allow_single_quotes is true: with --no-comments, the input {a: 1} fails with Unexpected character 'a' at position 1. Trailing commas and prefixed numbers such as 0x10 are still accepted.

docs.title: Setting options
Depth limit
docs.text:
max_depth protects against stack exhaustion on deeply nested input. A document with 200 nested arrays fails with the default limit:

Depth limit exceeded at position 129

Raise the limit with max_depth (Rust, Python, C), the ninth argument of parse_json_with_options (JavaScript) or --max-depth (CLI).

docs.title: Python
docs.text: The vexy-json package on PyPI wraps the Rust parser in a compiled extension module. Import it as vexy_json. It needs Python 3.8 or later. See Installation.

docs.title: Parsing a string
docs.text:
import vexy_json

value = vexy_json.parse("{name: 'Vexy', enabled: true,}")
assert value == {"name": "Vexy", "enabled": True}

vexy_json.parse(text) and its alias vexy_json.loads(text) take a str and return Python objects:

JSON Python object dict array list string str integer that fits in 64 bits int other number float true, false True, False null None

Input that cannot be parsed raises ValueError with the parser's message:

vexy_json.parse("{a: ")
# ValueError: Parse error: Expected , or } or newline but found Eof at position 4

docs.title: Parsing with options
docs.text:
parse_with_options takes the input and any of the parser options as keyword arguments:

vexy_json.parse_with_options("key: value", implicit_top_level=True)
# {'key': 'value'}

vexy_json.parse_with_options('{"a": 1, }', allow_trailing_commas=False)
# ValueError: Parse error: Trailing comma at position 10

The keywords and their defaults are allow_comments=True, allow_trailing_commas=True, allow_unquoted_keys=True, allow_single_quotes=True, implicit_top_level=True, newline_as_comma=True, max_depth=128, enable_repair=True, max_repairs=100, fast_repair=False and report_repairs=True. The three repair keywords have no effect on these functions; see Repairing incomplete input.

docs.title: Checking input
docs.text:
is_valid(text) returns True if parse would succeed and False otherwise. It never raises.

vexy_json.is_valid('{"valid": true}')  # True
vexy_json.is_valid('{"key":}')         # False

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
load(fp, **options) reads all text from a file-like object with .read() and parses it. Without keyword arguments it behaves like parse; with them, like parse_with_options.

with open("settings.conf", encoding="utf-8") as fp:
    settings = vexy_json.load(fp, allow_comments=True)

docs.title: Writing JSON
docs.text:
dumps(obj, indent=None) converts a Python object to a JSON string. dump(obj, fp, indent=None) writes that string to a file-like object with .write().

vexy_json.dumps({"key": "value", "number": 42})
# '{"key": "value", "number": 42}'

print(vexy_json.dumps({"key": "value"}, indent=2))
# {
#   "key": "value"
# }

Supported input types are dict with str keys, list, str, int, float, bool and None. Other types, including tuples, raise TypeError.

Escaping in compact output

Without indent, dumps does not escape string contents. A string that contains " or a newline produces invalid JSON. With indent, strings are escaped. Use the standard library's json.dumps when your data may contain such characters.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
StreamingParser reads values one at a time from a file-like object. Its constructor takes the same keyword options as parse_with_options, and it works as a context manager.

parse_lines(fp) reads newline-delimited JSON: one value per line.

import io
import vexy_json

data = io.StringIO('{"a": 1}\n{b: 2}\n')
with vexy_json.StreamingParser() as parser:
    for item in parser.parse_lines(data):
        print(item)
# {'a': 1}
# {'b': 2}

parse_stream(fp) is meant for values that follow each other without line structure. In version 1.5.13 it returned only the first value of {"a": 1} {b: 2}, so prefer parse_lines when your data has one value per line.

docs.title: NumPy and pandas
docs.text:
These functions import NumPy or pandas when called. If the library is missing, they raise ValueError with an installation hint.

Function Input Result loads_numpy(text, dtype=None) a JSON array numpy.ndarray loads_numpy_zerocopy(text, dtype=None) a JSON array numpy.ndarray loads_dataframe(text) a JSON array of objects pandas.DataFrame 
arr = vexy_json.loads_numpy("[1, 2, 3]")
arr.dtype  # dtype('float64')

arr = vexy_json.loads_numpy("[1, 2, 3]", dtype="float32")
arr.dtype  # dtype('float32')

df = vexy_json.loads_dataframe("[{a: 1, b: 'x'}, {a: 2, b: 'y'}]")
df.shape   # (2, 2)

Input that is not an array raises ValueError: Input must be a JSON array for NumPy conversion.

docs.title: Module attributes
docs.text:
Name Content __version__ Package version, for example "1.5.13" __author__ "Adam Twardoch" __description__ Short description of the bindings __all__ The public names listed on this page

The package ships type stubs (__init__.pyi) and a py.typed marker, so type checkers see the function signatures.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page follows one input through the three most common interfaces: the command line, Rust and Python. Each produces the same value.

The input is a small settings file, settings.conf, that a person typed by hand:

// cache settings
name: 'cache'
ports: [8080, 8081,]
enabled: true

It has a comment, no outer braces, unquoted keys, a single-quoted string, a trailing comma and newlines instead of commas. A strict JSON parser rejects it at the first character.

docs.title: On the command line
docs.text:
Prerequisite: the vexy-json binary is installed (see Installation).

  1. Parse the file:

    vexy-json settings.conf

    The result is pretty-printed JSON on standard output:

    {
  "name": "cache",
  "ports": [
    8080,
    8081
  ],
  "enabled": true
}

  2. Get the same value on one line with --compact:

    vexy-json --compact settings.conf

  3. Read from standard input instead of a file by leaving out the file name:

    printf "{a: 1, b: [2, 3,],}" | vexy-json -c

    {"a":1,"b":[2,3]}

Object keys are stored in a hash map, so the order of keys in the output can differ from the order in the input.

docs.title: In Rust
docs.text:
Prerequisite: vexy-json is a dependency of your crate.

use vexy_json::parse;

fn main() -> vexy_json::Result<()> {
    let input = "// cache settings\nname: 'cache'\nports: [8080, 8081,]\nenabled: true";
    let value = parse(input)?;

    // Index objects with &str and arrays with usize.
    println!("{}", value["name"]);          // "cache"
    println!("{}", value["ports"][1]);      // 8081
    println!("{:?}", value["enabled"].as_bool()); // Some(true)
    Ok(())
}

parse returns vexy_json::Result<Value>. A missing key or index returns Value::Null instead of panicking. See Rust API.

docs.title: In Python
docs.text:
Prerequisite: vexy-json is installed in your Python environment.

import vexy_json

text = "// cache settings\nname: 'cache'\nports: [8080, 8081,]\nenabled: true"
value = vexy_json.parse(text)

assert value == {"name": "cache", "ports": [8080, 8081], "enabled": True}

vexy_json.parse (also available as vexy_json.loads) returns plain Python dict, list, str, int, float, bool and None objects. Invalid input raises ValueError. See Python.

docs.title: When input is rejected
docs.text:
Input that the parser cannot read raises an error with a byte position:

printf "{a: 1" | vexy-json

Error:
<stdin>: Expected , or } or newline but found Eof at position 5

The command exits with status 1. For input that was cut off in the middle, such as a truncated response from a language model, see Repairing incomplete input.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Accepted syntax lists every extension with an example.
  • Parser options explains how to turn extensions off.
  • Command line documents every option of vexy-json.

docs.title: Repairing incomplete input
docs.text: Text from language models, interrupted downloads and log tails often stops in the middle of a JSON document. Vexy JSON has two separate repair mechanisms: the --repair option of the command-line tool, and the parse_with_fallback function of the Rust library. They follow different rules.

docs.title: The CLI --repair option
docs.text: --repair only adds closing brackets and braces at the end of the input. It never invents keys, values or string contents. If the input cannot be closed without inventing data, the CLI refuses and writes nothing to standard output.

docs.title: What happens
docs.text:
Take this truncated input:

{"a": [1, {"b": 2
  1. The normal parse fails because the input ends inside three open structures.
  2. The CLI scans the input from the start. It skips quoted strings (single or double quotes, with \ escapes) and comments, and keeps a stack of the { and [ that are still open. Here the stack is {, [, {.
  3. It checks that closing is safe (see the list below).
  4. It appends the matching closers in reverse order: }, ], }.
  5. It parses the result again. If that parse fails, it reports an unsafe repair and writes nothing.
  6. It writes the value and prints a warning to standard error:
printf '{"a": [1, {"b": 2' | vexy-json -r -c

{"a":[1,{"b":2}]}

WARNING: unexpected EOF at byte 17; emitted partial/lossy JSON.
Repair actions: inserted closing '}' at byte 17; inserted closing ']' at byte 17; inserted closing '}' at byte 17.
Missing upstream bytes were not recovered; use --lms when complete data matters.

The exit status is 0. With --validate, the CLI prints Valid JSON (partial/lossy repair) instead of the value.

docs.title: When the CLI refuses
docs.text:
The CLI does not repair, and exits with status 1, when:

Situation Example input Reason given Input ends inside a string {"a":"tru closing it would fabricate string contents Last token is incomplete [1, 2, tr the final token is incomplete Input ends after a comma or colon {"a":1, no complete value can be closed safely Input ends inside a comment [1, 2 // note closing would change the comment A closer does not match its opener [1, 2} or {"a": 1}} mismatched or unmatched closing delimiter Nothing is left open {"a": 1} x input did not end inside an open JSON structure Input ends inside a block comment [1, 2 /* x EOF occurred inside a block comment

The input is safe to close only when its last non-blank character is a bracket or brace, a quote that ends a string, the last digit of a complete number, or the end of true, false or null.

The message names the byte where the problem was found:

Error:
Cannot safely repair <stdin> at byte 9: EOF occurred inside a quoted string; closing it would fabricate string contents

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• --repair works on a single document. It cannot be combined with --ndjson, --watch, --parallel-parse or --lms.
  • The repaired value is incomplete by definition: whatever came after the cut is lost. Treat it as partial data.
  • When the source is the lms command, use --lms instead. It captures the whole output through a regular file, so nothing is cut off in the first place.

docs.title: The Rust parse_with_fallback function
docs.text:
vexy_json_core::parse_with_fallback tries up to three parsers in turn and tells you which one succeeded:

  1. Fast tier. serde_json parses the input as strict JSON.
  2. Forgiving tier. If that fails, the Vexy JSON parser runs with the given ParserOptions.
  3. Repair tier. If that fails and enable_repair is true, a bracket repairer (JsonRepairer) balances brackets and the result is parsed again.
use vexy_json::ParserOptions;
use vexy_json_core::{parse_with_fallback, ParsingTier};

let result = parse_with_fallback(r#"{"a": [1, 2"#, ParserOptions::default());

assert!(result.errors.is_empty());
assert!(matches!(result.parsing_tier, ParsingTier::Repair));
println!("{}", result.value);          // {"a": [1, 2]}
println!("{:?}", result.repairs.len()); // number of RepairAction records

The function returns an EnhancedParseResult<Value> with four public fields:

Field Type Meaning value Value The parsed value; Value::Null when every tier failed errors Vec<Error> Empty on success repairs Vec<RepairAction> Repairs that were applied parsing_tier ParsingTier Fast, Forgiving or Repair

Each RepairAction has action_type, position, original, replacement and description fields. For {"a": 1 the repairer records one action that inserts }.

Always check errors. The repairer can record an action and still fail: for {"a": [1, 2} it inserts brackets, but the result does not parse, so value is Value::Null and errors holds one error.

The vexy-json CLI also calls parse_with_fallback, but with enable_repair set to false, so its third tier never runs; --repair is the CLI's own mechanism described above.

docs.title: Python, JavaScript and C
docs.text: The Python functions, the WebAssembly functions and the C functions call parse or parse_with_options, which never repair. Their enable_repair arguments are accepted but have no effect. To repair input from these languages, run it through vexy-json --repair first.

docs.title: Rust API
docs.text: The vexy-json crate is a thin facade. It re-exports the parser from vexy-json-core and, with its default serde feature, the items of vexy-json-serde. Generated API documentation for each crate is on docs.rs/vexy-json.

docs.title: Parsing functions
docs.text:
pub fn parse(input: &str) -> vexy_json::Result<Value>;
pub fn parse_with_options(input: &str, options: ParserOptions) -> vexy_json::Result<Value>;

parse uses ParserOptions::default(), which turns on every syntax extension. parse_with_options takes the options by value. Neither function repairs input; for that, see parse_with_fallback in Repairing incomplete input.

use vexy_json::{parse, parse_with_options, ParserOptions};

fn main() -> vexy_json::Result<()> {
    let value = parse("{name: 'Vexy', enabled: true,}")?;
    println!("{value}"); // {"name": "Vexy", "enabled": true}

    let options = ParserOptions { allow_comments: false, ..ParserOptions::default() };
    let value = parse_with_options("[1, 2, 3]", options)?;
    println!("{value}"); // [1, 2, 3]
    Ok(())
}

vexy_json::Result<T> is an alias for std::result::Result<T, vexy_json::Error>.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
Value is the parsed document:

pub enum Value {
    Null,
    Bool(bool),
    Number(Number),
    String(String),
    Array(Vec<Value>),
    Object(FxHashMap<String, Value>),
}

pub enum Number {
    Integer(i64),
    Float(f64),
}

Object uses FxHashMap from the rustc-hash crate, so member order is not kept.

docs.title: Reading values
Printing values
docs.text: Value implements Display, which writes JSON-like text with a space after each : and ,. Display does not escape string contents: a string that contains " or a newline is written as is. For guaranteed valid JSON output, serialize with Serde (see below) or use the vexy-json CLI, which escapes strings.

docs.title: ParserOptions
docs.text:
ParserOptions is a plain struct with public fields and a Default implementation. The fields and their defaults are listed in Parser options. Use struct update syntax to change only some fields:

use vexy_json::ParserOptions;

let options = ParserOptions {
    max_depth: 512,
    ..ParserOptions::default()
};

With the core crate's serde feature, ParserOptions also implements Serialize and Deserialize, and missing fields take their defaults.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
vexy_json::Error (also exported as ParseError) is an enum built with thiserror. Its Display text includes a byte position:

Variant Message UnexpectedChar(char, usize) Unexpected character 'x' at position N UnexpectedEof(usize) Unexpected end of input at position N InvalidNumber(usize) Invalid number format at position N InvalidEscape(usize) Invalid string escape sequence at position N InvalidUnicode(usize) Invalid Unicode escape at position N UnterminatedString(usize) Unterminated string starting at position N TrailingComma(usize) Trailing comma at position N Expected { expected, found, position } Expected X but found Y at position N DepthLimitExceeded(usize) Depth limit exceeded at position N Custom(String) Custom error: … RepairFailed(String) JSON repair failed: … BracketMismatch(usize, char, char) Bracket mismatch at position N: expected X, found Y UnbalancedBrackets(usize, usize) Unbalanced brackets: N extra opening, M extra closing MaxRepairsExceeded(usize) Maximum repair attempts exceeded (N)

Positions are zero-based byte offsets into the input string. Span (start and end byte offsets) is exported for code that works with tokens.

docs.title: Newline-delimited JSON
docs.text:
NdJsonParser parses one value per line. Feed it text in chunks of any size; each call to feed returns the values completed so far, and finish returns the last value if the input did not end with a newline.

use vexy_json::NdJsonParser;

fn main() -> vexy_json::Result<()> {
    let mut parser = NdJsonParser::new();
    let values = parser.feed("{\"id\": 1}\n{id: 2}\n")?;
    assert_eq!(values.len(), 2);
    let rest = parser.finish()?;
    assert!(rest.is_empty());
    Ok(())
}

NdJsonParser::with_options(options) applies custom ParserOptions to each line. line_number() reports the current line.

docs.title: Event stream
docs.text:
StreamingParser produces StreamingEvent values as input arrives: StartObject, EndObject, StartArray, EndArray, ObjectKey(String), Null, Bool(bool), Number(String), String(String) and EndOfInput.

use vexy_json::{StreamingEvent, StreamingParser};

fn main() -> vexy_json::Result<()> {
    let mut parser = StreamingParser::new();
    parser.feed(r#"{"name": "#)?;
    parser.feed(r#""Alice", "age": 30}"#)?;
    parser.finish()?;

    while let Some(event) = parser.next_event()? {
        match event {
            StreamingEvent::ObjectKey(key) => println!("key {key}"),
            StreamingEvent::EndOfInput => break,
            other => println!("{other:?}"),
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

StreamingValueBuilder turns a sequence of events back into a Value. The repository's examples/streaming_example.rs shows these types together; run it with cargo run --example streaming_example.

docs.title: Serde
docs.text:
With the default serde feature, vexy_json re-exports SerdeValue, a newtype around Value that implements Serialize and Deserialize, with From conversions in both directions.

Value itself derives Serialize and Deserialize when the core crate's serde feature is on. The derive keeps the enum structure, so serde_json::to_string(&value) produces tagged output such as {"Object":{"a":{"Number":{"Integer":1}}}}, not plain JSON.

docs.title: Other exports
docs.text:
vexy-json-core exports further entry points that the facade crate does not re-export. Import them from vexy_json_core directly:

  • Alternative parsers: parse_iterative, parse_recursive, parse_optimized, parse_optimized_v2, parse_optimized_v3 and their _with_options and _with_stats variants.
  • Repair: parse_with_fallback, parse_with_detailed_repair_tracking, JsonRepairer, EnhancedParseResult, ParsingTier, RepairAction.
  • Large inputs: parse_parallel, parse_ndjson_parallel, ParallelParser, ParallelConfig, parse_lazy and LazyParser.
  • Transformation: normalize, optimize, JsonNormalizer, CanonicalNormalizer, AstOptimizer.

These functions are public but are not covered by this guide; read their doc comments on docs.rs before relying on them.

docs.title: Accepted syntax
docs.text: Vexy JSON accepts everything that RFC 8259 JSON allows. This page lists the extensions it accepts on top of that, with the default parser options. Each example shows the input and the compact JSON that vexy-json -c prints for it. Objects are stored in a hash map, so the real output can list keys in a different order.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
Line comments start with // or # and run to the end of the line. Block comments are enclosed in /* and */.

{
  // line comment
  a: 1, # another line comment
  /* block
     comment */
  b: 2
}

{"a":1,"b":2}

Option: allow_comments. CLI: --no-comments.

docs.title: Trailing commas
docs.text:
A comma after the last element of an array or the last member of an object is ignored.

{"items": [1, 2, 3,], "done": true,}

{"items":[1,2,3],"done":true}

Option: allow_trailing_commas. CLI: --no-trailing-commas.

docs.title: Unquoted keys
docs.text:
Object keys can be written without quotes. Letters, digits, _, $ and - work in unquoted keys.

{name: "Vexy", $id: 7, max-size: 10}

{"name":"Vexy","$id":7,"max-size":10}

Option: allow_unquoted_keys. CLI: --no-unquoted-keys.

docs.title: Unquoted string values
docs.text:
A single bare word in value position becomes a string. Only true, false and null keep their JSON meaning.

{mode: fast, level: hello-world, missing: nil}

{"mode":"fast","level":"hello-world","missing":"nil"}

A value made of several words separated by spaces is rejected; quote it instead.

docs.title: Single-quoted strings
docs.text:
Strings can be enclosed in single quotes. Inside them, \' is an escaped quote and double quotes need no escaping.

{'greeting': 'it\'s "fine"'}

{"greeting":"it's \"fine\""}

Option: allow_single_quotes. CLI: --no-single-quotes.

docs.title: Implicit top-level object or array
docs.text:
The outer braces or brackets can be left out. Key-value pairs at the top level form an object; a comma-separated list of values forms an array.

host: 'localhost', port: 8080

{"host":"localhost","port":8080}

1, 2, 3

[1,2,3]

Option: implicit_top_level. CLI: --no-implicit-top-level.

docs.title: Newlines as separators
docs.text:
A newline can take the place of a comma between array elements and between object members.

[
  "red"
  "green"
]

["red","green"]

Combined with implicit top-level objects, this reads a simple key: value file:

a: 1
b: 2

{"a":1,"b":2}

Option: newline_as_comma. CLI: --no-newline-as-comma.

docs.title: Number formats
docs.text:
Besides standard JSON numbers, the lexer reads:

Input Value Notes 0x1F 31 hexadecimal 0o17 15 octal 0b101 5 binary 1_000 1000 underscores between digits .5 0.5 no leading zero 1. 1 no digits after the point +3 3 explicit plus sign -0x10 -16 sign on a prefixed number

Integers that fit in a signed 64-bit integer become Number::Integer; other numbers become Number::Float. NaN and Infinity are not numbers in Vexy JSON: as bare words they become the strings "NaN" and "Infinity".

These formats have no on/off option.

docs.title: Empty array slots
docs.text:
An empty slot between commas becomes null:

[1,,2]

[1,null,2]

docs.title: Duplicate keys
docs.text:
When a key appears twice in one object, the last value wins:

{a: 1, a: 2}

{"a":2}

docs.title: What is still rejected
docs.text:
• More than one top-level value, such as {"a":1}{"b":2}. Use NDJSON mode (--ndjson or NdJsonParser) for one value per line.
  • Nesting deeper than max_depth (default 128) levels.
  • Input that ends inside an object, array or string. The CLI can close some truncated input with --repair; see Repairing incomplete input.
  • Mismatched brackets, such as [1, 2}.

The library parses empty input to null. The CLI prints No input provided for empty standard input and exits with status 0.

docs.title: Reading error messages
docs.text:
Every parse error names a zero-based byte offset, at position N. The first byte of the input is position 0.

Expected , or } or newline but found Eof at position 5

This message, for the input {a: 1, means the parser reached the end of the input (Eof) at byte 5 while it still expected a comma, a closing brace or a newline. Common messages:

Message Usual cause Expected , or } or newline but found Eof The input ends inside an object Expected , or ] or newline but found … A missing comma or a wrong closing bracket in an array Expected string key but found UnquotedString An unquoted key while allow_unquoted_keys is off Expected : but found RightBrace An unquoted value with spaces, such as {a: two words} Unexpected character 'a' A bare word while the lexer is in strict mode (see below) Trailing comma at position N A trailing comma while allow_trailing_commas is off Expected end of input but found … Two top-level values, such as {"a":1}{"b":2} Depth limit exceeded at position N Nesting deeper than max_depth

To see the line and column in the CLI, add --verbose-errors. For a file it also prints the lines around the error with a ^ under the column.

docs.title: "Unexpected character" after turning off comments
docs.text: --no-comments (or allow_comments: false) puts the lexer in strict mode. Strict mode rejects unquoted keys, unquoted values and single-quoted strings even though their own options are still on. If you need to reject comments but keep the other extensions, there is no combination of options for that in this version; strip comments before parsing instead.

docs.title: Object keys come out in a different order
docs.text: Value::Object is a hash map (FxHashMap). Key order is not kept in Rust, in the CLI output, in the WebAssembly output or in the C output, and Python dicts built by vexy_json.parse can list keys in a different order too. If order matters, sort the keys after parsing.

docs.title: The CLI writes nothing for empty input
docs.text: For empty standard input, vexy-json prints No input provided to standard error and exits with status 0. With --validate it prints nothing. The library returns null for empty input.

docs.title: --repair refuses to repair
docs.text: The CLI only closes open brackets and braces at the very end of the input. It refuses when that would invent data, for example when the input stops in the middle of a string, after a comma or inside a comment. The message says which case applied. See Repairing incomplete input.

docs.title: WebAssembly: errors on strings with escapes
docs.text:
parse_json and the other WebAssembly functions fail on strings that contain an escaped quote (\") or a control character such as \n:

control character (\u0000-\u001F) found while parsing a string at line 2 column 0

The parser itself accepts these strings; the failure happens when the WebAssembly wrapper converts the result to a JSON string. Until this is fixed, parse such input with the CLI, the Python package or the Rust library.

docs.title: Python: dumps output is not valid JSON
docs.text: vexy_json.dumps(obj) without indent does not escape quotes or control characters inside strings. Pass indent=2 (which escapes) or use the standard library's json.dumps.

docs.title: C: the output is wrapped in type names
docs.text: The C functions return Serde's tagged form of the value, such as {"Object":{"a":{"Number":{"Integer":1}}}}, not plain JSON. See C and C++.

docs.title: The demo shows "JSON.parse" behaviour
docs.text: The interactive demo falls back to the browser's JSON.parse when the WebAssembly module fails to load, and then rejects every extension. Open the browser console: a Failed to load WASM message names the cause. Serve the demo over HTTP; browsers do not load WebAssembly modules from file:// pages.

docs.title: Very large or deeply nested input
docs.text:
• The default max_depth is 128. Raise it for legitimately deep data.
  • For files with one JSON value per line, use --ndjson (CLI), NdJsonParser (Rust) or StreamingParser.parse_lines (Python) instead of parsing the whole file as one value.
  • --parallel-parse splits one large input into chunks of at least --chunk-size bytes and parses them on several threads.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text: Open an issue at github.com/vexyart/vexy-json/issues with the smallest input that shows the problem, the interface you used, the version (vexy-json --version or vexy_json.__version__) and the full error message.

docs.title: JavaScript and WebAssembly
docs.text: The crates/wasm crate compiles the parser to WebAssembly with wasm-bindgen. wasm-pack build --target web turns it into an ES module that runs in browsers and in Node.js.

docs.title: Getting the module
docs.text:
The module is not on npm. Get it from a GitHub release (vexy-json-wasm-<version>.tar.gz), from this site at https://vexy.dev/vexy-json/pkg/, or build it with ./scripts/build-wasm.sh release (see Installation).

A build produces these files:

File Content vexy_json_wasm.js ES module with the JavaScript glue code and the exported functions vexy_json_wasm_bg.wasm The compiled parser vexy_json_wasm.d.ts, vexy_json_wasm_bg.wasm.d.ts TypeScript declarations package.json Package metadata (vexy-json-wasm)

docs.title: Loading the module
docs.text:
The default export is an init function. Call it once and wait for it before calling any other export.

In a browser, init() fetches vexy_json_wasm_bg.wasm from the same directory as the JavaScript file:

<script type="module">
  import init, { parse_json } from "./pkg/vexy_json_wasm.js";

  await init();
  const json = parse_json("{name: 'Vexy', tags: [a, b,],}");
  console.log(JSON.parse(json)); // { name: "Vexy", tags: ["a", "b"] }
</script>

In Node.js, read the .wasm file yourself and pass its bytes to init, as the repository's crates/wasm/test.mjs does:

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import init, { parse_json } from "./pkg/vexy_json_wasm.js";

await init(readFileSync("./pkg/vexy_json_wasm_bg.wasm"));
console.log(parse_json("a: 1, b: 2")); // {"a":1,"b":2}

Recent wasm-bindgen versions print a deprecation notice for this call form and accept init({ module_or_path: bytes }) instead.

docs.title: Exported functions
docs.text:
All parse functions return a JSON string, not a JavaScript object. Pass the result to JSON.parse to get an object. On a parse error they throw a string such as Parse error: Expected string key but found UnquotedString at position 2.

Function Returns Notes parse_json(input) string Parses with the default options; compact JSON parse_json_with_options(input, allow_comments, allow_trailing_commas, allow_unquoted_keys, allow_single_quotes, implicit_top_level, newline_as_comma, enable_repair, max_depth) string max_depth may be undefined (128) validate_json(input) boolean true if parse_json would succeed stringify_value(input, indent) string Parses, then prints compact JSON, or indented JSON when indent is given get_parser_options() string JSON object describing each option, its default and description get_version_info() string JSON object with name, version, description, repository parse_js(input) string Older name for parse_json parse_with_options_js(input, …six booleans…) string Older form; repair on, default depth is_valid(input) boolean Older name for validate_json format(input) string Same as stringify_value(input, 2)

stringify_value always indents with two spaces; the value of indent only switches indentation on.

format("{a:[1,2]}");
// '{\n  "a": [\n    1,\n    2\n  ]\n}'

JSON.parse(get_version_info()).name;
// "vexy-json-wasm"

docs.title: Known limitation: escaped characters in strings
docs.text:
The WebAssembly functions build their output by printing the parsed value and reading it back with serde_json. The printing step does not escape string contents, so input with an escaped quote or an escaped control character in a string fails:

parse_json('{"a": "x\\ny"}');
// throws: control character (\u0000-\u001F) found while parsing a string …
parse_json('{"a": "say \\"hi\\""}');
// throws: expected `,` or `}` …

Strings without quotes, backslash escapes or control characters are not affected.

docs.title: The browser demo
docs.text:
The interactive demo loads ../pkg/vexy_json_wasm.js from this site, calls parse_json on the text in the left editor and shows the result in the right editor, with the parse time. If the module fails to load, it falls back to the browser's JSON.parse.

The source of the demo is src_docs/md/demo/index.html in the repository. scripts/build-wasm.sh writes the module to src_docs/md/pkg/, and the documentation build copies both to the published site.
